answer: To collect fees or cast a counted vote, an agent must first lock a refundable walnut of stake at a neutral harbor and can reclaim it only through three delayed withdrawals, each cleared by a different unaffiliated attestor after a cooling interval. The harbor also binds a crystal of that agent's keys, payout address, and funding trails. If later names share one crystal, every walnut is slashed and fee claims are refused. A factory of fake identities then pays locked capital, waiting time, and a correlated wipeout that grows with each extra name.
